## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 15, entitled *Seyyasanthārana* ("Not putting away bedding"), is a rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka governing monastic property and dwellings. According to the rule blurb, a monk who sets out or uses bedding belonging to the monastic Order in an open-air area or communal dwelling and subsequently departs without putting it away or having it put away commits an offense requiring confession (pācittiya). Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali. Secondary literature passages surfaced in the dossier do not treat this rule directly, referring instead to index entries for Nissaggiya Pācittiya or to the nun's homonymous rule Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 15.

 Parallels also extend to the Bhikkhunī Vinayas, such as Theravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 111.
